GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2014-11-05T13:11:43Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Incoherence: different sort behaviour when setting models and collections
Description: Let's assume a collection is sorted by an attribute called `name`. In other words, its `comparator` is `'name'`. 

_Model behaviour_: If we take one of the collection's models and `set` the `name` attribute, the collection will not be re-sorted and no `sort` event will be triggered. This is well explained in the documentation.

_Collection behaviour_: Now, if we take the collection as a whole and call `set` on it, passing it the existing model but with a modified `name`, it will indeed re-sort the collection and trigger a `sort` event; refer to the following line:

``` javascript
if (sortable && !sort && existing.hasChanged(sortAttr)) sort = true;
```

Is this intended? IMHO, it would be better if either both of them caused a re-sort, or none of them.
